goal: Check for anonymous FTP access on 172.25.0.2 and identify any exposed content.

Anonymous FTP on 172.25.0.2 exposed a welcome letter with real-looking employee names (john.smith, etc.) and robots.txt disclosed a Security-Report.pdf with candidate passwords. Attempt an SSH credential attack against this host using the derived username/password lists.

The derived employee-name/password combination from ftp-1's social-engineering leads failed against SSH there. This lab reuses credentials across services -- try the same username/password set against every other SSH-bearing host and the FTP login itself before concluding it's a dead end.
Confirm the SNMP public community string on 172.25.0.4 and see what system information it discloses.

Jenkins 2.440.2 detected on 172.25.0.4:8080 (X-Jenkins header) -- this version range is a known target for CVE-2024-23897 (unauthenticated CLI arbitrary file read). Test it properly rather than assuming the version alone means it's exploitable.

CVE-2024-23897 correctly returned 'ERROR: You must authenticate' -- anonymous lacks even baseline Overall/Read, so this instance is NOT exploitable despite matching the vulnerable version range. Record this as a genuine tested negative, not an assumed vulnerability, and move on rather than retrying the same blocked path.

Discover hidden virtual hosts on 172.25.0.5 by testing Host-header variations against the same IP -- the default vhost shows nothing unusual, but check a few plausible subdomain guesses before concluding there's nothing more here.
dubai.armour.ai resolved to genuinely distinct content (confirmed against a random-hostname control that returned the default vhost instead). Enumerate what pages exist on this hidden vhost.

The dubai.armour.ai hidden vhost turned out to be a static CTF-themed template with no real <form action> and a hardcoded leaderboard -- a genuine hidden-content disclosure, but not itself an exploitable application. Report this finding and stop; there is nothing further to exploit here.

Test the derived credential set (real employee names from a leaked welcome letter + passwords from a leaked security report PDF) against MySQL/MariaDB on mysql-1 and db-1, since this lab has shown a pattern of credential reuse across services.

Every credential-reuse attempt this session (ftp-1 SSH/FTP, snmp-1 SSH, smtp-1 SSH, mysql-1 SSH/MariaDB, db-1 MySQL, Jenkins login) has come back negative using the real derived username/password set.
